description: FACTS, the Framework for Assessing Changes To Sea-level, is a modular system for global mean, regional and extreme sea-level projection. Rutgers researchers publish code and documentation for combining processes at different complexity levels and exploring uncertainty in future sea level. Users choose physical components, emissions or climate scenarios, locations and ensemble settings; outputs are projected sea-level distributions or trajectories for the chosen sites and time horizons. Geographic coverage can be global or regional and is determined by the selected modules. MIT-licensed source and documentation are publicly available. A limitation is that different scientific choices can produce materially different projections; the framework is designed to expose that ambiguity, not settle it. FACTS can supply coastal-flood and port-risk scenarios for infrastructure simulation. The catalogue's data-ipcc-ar6-sea-level-projections is a separate published projection product for comparison, not a FACTS input by default. No model run or projection dataset was downloaded.
